greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who stands with us in every trial, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the victor over every fear: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you give us the wisdom of the Spirit: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you promise that not a hair on our head is lost to your love: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Great and wonderful are all your works, Lord God almighty.
homily:
We often imagine the victory of God as a sudden, thunderous event—a moment where the clouds part, the noise of the world is silenced, and the triumph of light over darkness is made plain for all to see. We look for a victory that feels like a completed project, a finished line of code, or a destination reached after a long, weary flight. But the Book of Revelation gives us a different image of victory. John sees a sea of glass mingled with fire. It is a place of standing. It is a place of song. Those who have won the victory are not sitting in an easy chair; they are standing on the edge of a vast, shimmering expanse, holding harps, singing the song of the Lamb. 

I want you to hold onto this image: the sea of glass mingled with fire. It is a place where the clarity of heaven meets the refining heat of human experience. Think of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way he moved through his fifteen years. He was a boy who loved the mechanics of the world—the way a plane lifts off the runway, the logic of a complex system, the beauty of a well-structured plan. He was a boy who looked at the horizon and saw potential, who dreamed of 'con chim airlines' with a giggle and a sparkle in his eye. He was a boy who lived with a vibrant, restless curiosity, always reaching for the next discovery. But beneath that brilliant mind was a heart that was being tempered by love. He was a boy who understood that to live is to be in motion, to be moving toward a destination, even when the path is not entirely clear. He was a boy who lived his life like a pilot, steady at the controls, always looking forward, always trusting that there was a place to land.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: five months have passed. The calendar page turns, but the heart often stays in the room where he last smiled. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the quick laugh, the bright smile, the way he would share his dreams of the future—are suddenly met with an empty space. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ambush of sorrow when you least expect it. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are not a lack of faith; they are the language of love that has no place left to go.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s living. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus tells his disciples, 'They will seize and persecute you... it will lead to your giving testimony.' He does not promise an easy path. He promises that when the world tries to shake us, he will give us a wisdom that our adversaries cannot resist. This is the hinge of the mystery. We think our testimony is what we say, but our true testimony is who we are in the presence of the Lord. Think of Benjamin’s heart—that boy who, unprompted, wanted to hand over his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it; the offering itself was the testimony. It was the pure, unadulterated desire to be a blessing to someone else. That is the wisdom that cannot be refuted. That is the life that speaks louder than any argument. Ben’s life is a testimony that love is the only thing that survives the fire. The sea of glass is mingled with fire because the love we give on earth is the only thing that remains when we pass through the veil. It is purified, it is made eternal, and it is what we carry into the presence of the Lamb.

Consider the image of the sea of glass again. It is a place of reflection. When you look at the life of your son, your brother, your friend, you are looking into the sea of God’s own heart. You are seeing the reflection of a boy who was a gift, a boy who lived with a radiant, cheerful smile, even when he was just a baby in a lime-green cape, even when he was a teenager looking out from an airplane window. He was a boy who knew, in his own way, that he was loved. He is standing on that sea now. He is part of the great multitude. He is fully alive, fully restored, and fully embraced by the Father. He is the boy who loved to dream, the boy who giggled at the idea of his own airline, the boy who looked at the world with such profound curiosity. He is all of that, and he is with the God of the living. He is the firstfruits of the promise, waiting for the day when the family of four is whole again. He is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where you and Ben were standing outside room 419, and he said with that earnest, familiar voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart. You are the one who carries his laughter forward. You are the one who keeps the melody alive.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. The Lamb who was slain is the Lamb who is risen, and he is the one who promises that one day, every tear will be wiped away, and we will see clearly that love was the only thing that ever mattered. The God of the living is the God who is with you right now in this very room, in the silence, in the ache, and in the hope that refuses to die. 

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest in the eternal light and peace of Christ, we pray to the Lord.
For all who are grieving and carrying the weight of loss, that God may console their hearts, strengthen their hope, and remind them that they are never alone, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
I, John, saw in heaven another sign, great and awe-inspiring:
seven angels with the seven last plagues,
for through them God’s fury is accomplished.

Then I saw something like a sea of glass mingled with fire.
On the sea of glass were standing those
who had won the victory over the beast
and its image and the number that signified its name.
They were holding God’s harps,
and they sang the song of Moses, the servant of God,
and the song of the Lamb:

“Great and wonderful are your works,
Lord God almighty.
Just and true are your ways,
O king of the nations.
Who will not fear you, Lord,
or glorify your name?
For you alone are holy.
All the nations will come
and worship before you,
for your righteous acts have been revealed.”

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to the crowd:
“They will seize and persecute you,
they will hand you over to the synagogues and to prisons,
and they will have you led before kings and governors
because of my name.
It will lead to your giving testimony.
Remember, you are not to prepare your defense beforehand,
for I myself shall give you a wisdom in speaking
that all your adversaries will be powerless to resist or refute.
You will even be handed over by parents,
brothers, relatives, and friends,
and they will put some of you to death.
You will be hated by all because of my name,
but not a hair on your head will be destroyed.
By your perseverance you will secure your lives.”

day: Wednesday of the Thirty-fourth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
